title: Data Augmentation for Images 🎨
description: Artificially expand your dataset with rotations, flips, zooms, and more.

slides.title: More Data = Better Model 📈
slides.content:
# But Collecting Real Data is Expensive

**Data augmentation** generates new training samples from existing ones by applying random transformations:

- Rotation, shift, shear, zoom
- Flip horizontally/vertically
- Brightness/contrast adjustments

All these preserve the label (a rotated cat is still a cat).

slides.title: ImageDataGenerator (Legacy) & Preprocessing Layers
slides.content: TF 2.x offers `tf.keras.layers.RandomFlip`, `RandomRotation`, etc., as part of the model or `tf.keras.preprocessing.image.ImageDataGenerator` for on‑the‑fly augmentation.
slides.codeSnippet:
from tensorflow.keras.layers import RandomFlip, RandomRotation

data_augmentation = Sequential([
    RandomFlip('horizontal'),
    RandomRotation(0.1),
])

quizData.question: Data augmentation is only applied during training, not validation/testing.
quizData.explanation: Augmentation artificially increases training variety; evaluation should be on original, unaugmented data.

slides.title: Common Augmentations 🛠️
slides.content:
# Visual Examples
- **RandomFlip('horizontal')**: mirrors image left‑right.
- **RandomRotation(0.2)**: rotate by random angle up to 0.2*2π (~72°).
- **RandomZoom(0.2)**: zoom in/out by ±20%.
- **RandomContrast(0.2)**: adjust contrast.

You can compose them in a Sequential model and apply as part of the data pipeline or inside the model itself.

slides.title: Integrating Augmentation into the Model
slides.content: Place augmentation layers at the very beginning:
slides.codeSnippet:
model = Sequential([
    RandomFlip('horizontal', input_shape=(32,32,3)),
    RandomRotation(0.1),
    Conv2D(32, (3,3), activation='relu'),
    # ... rest of CNN
])

slides.title: Be Careful with Augmentation ⚠️
slides.content: Don't augment validation/test data. Also, avoid transformations that change the label (e.g., vertical flip of a digit '6' becomes '9').
